title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
A synthetic media generation system created deepfake pornographic videos depicting Dutch public figures without their consent. The videos were hosted on a platform accessible to millions of monthly visitors, where they remained available despite being illegal under revenge porn laws. The system was deployed with no safeguard to prevent its use for non-consensual intimate imagery.

The failure was one of access control in a generative system. Someone with knowledge of how to operate the technology chose to use it for impersonation and harassment. It is not established whether the platform operators knew the content violated laws before being notified, or what measures they took to remove it once complaints were filed.

This case shows why generative systems capable of creating intimate imagery require deployment restrictions that go beyond terms of service. Human review before publication, age verification, identity confirmation, or restricted access could have prevented the videos from reaching an audience. The system itself functioned as designed, but was used in a context its creators should have anticipated and prevented.

summary:
Several well-known Dutch female celebrities are considering filing complaints after discovering they appear in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The platform hosts numerous fake videos featuring Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government ministers, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to report them, while managers and representatives of various victims confirmed to the news outlet that they have filed complaints or are considering legal action.

Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. Users who upload this material are advised to remain anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution, and earn money based on video views. Advocates warn that without government intervention, more fake videos featuring celebrities will continue to appear. Victims have several options including filing reports with the public prosecutor, starting a mass lawsuit, submitting complaints to the data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. In a previous case, presenter Welmoed Sijtsma made a documentary about her experience, and a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort received a conditional sentence of 180 hours in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
